nextRevision.basis: The 22 October 2019 notification adds dearness allowance twice a year, on 1 April and 1 October, from the six-monthly average consumer price index. The Labour Department's current-rates page, last checked on 29 October 2026, lists no order after the one effective from 1 April 2025, so the revisions due on 1 October 2025, 1 April 2026 and 1 October 2026 had not been published by then.

sources.legalBasis: Minimum Wages Act, 1948, section 5(2), after the Minimum Wages Advisory Board under section 7, on the Supreme Court's order of 31 October 2018 in SLP 26185-26228 of 2018. Applies to the classes of workers in all the scheduled employments of notification F.12(1)142/11/MW/Lab/2023-2047 of 26 July 2011. DA orders cite the department's order on it as 12(142)/02/MW/VII/3636.

tables.vdaNote: Delhi's order gives the rate in force and the DA added at each revision. Here, the base is the rate fixed by the 22 October 2019 notification, and DA is everything added since.

groups.title: All 25 scheduled employments
employments: Construction and maintenance of roads, and building operations
Metal working, except foundries and automobile engineering workshops
Textiles, including hosiery, niwar, handloom, lace, thread, name labels, and dyeing and printing
Plastic, rubber and PVC, including cables
Shops and establishments under the Delhi Shops and Establishments Act, 1954, including hotels, restaurants and cinemas, not covered by another employment
Bakery, confectionery, dairy products, fruit and food processing, fruit juices and aerated drinks
Radio, television, sound equipment, electrical appliances and electronic components
Every factory not covered by another employment
groups.note: The 2019 notification fixed one set of rates for every employment on Delhi's list of 26 July 2011. Brick kilns, domestic work and sales promotion are not on the list. Work for the central government, such as railways, mines, banks, central public sector companies and cantonments, follows the Centre's minimum wages, not Delhi's.

2026-10-16: da15april2025.pdf (text layer) read in full. Rates from 01.04.2025: unskilled 18456 per month and 710 per day, semi-skilled 20371 and 784, skilled 22411 and 862; clerical non-matriculate 20371 and 784, matriculate not graduate 22411 and 862, graduate and above 24356 and 937. 2026-10-16, corrected 2026-10-17: 5da.pdf (order 12(142)/02/MW/VII/3636, signed 23/10/2019; page 2 read by eye at 100 dpi). Its figures 14806, 16284, 17924 (clerical 16284, 17924, 19522) sit in the column 'Minimum Wages after adding DA w.e.f. 01.10.2019 to 22.10.2019 / date of notification': the 2017 rates plus DA, paid up to the notification. 2026-10-16: da_oct_2024.pdf (scanned, OCR and checked by eye). Rates as on 01.04.2024: 17988, 19825, 21813. From 01.10.2024: 18066 and 695, 19929 and 767, 21917 and 843; clerical 19929, 21917, 23836. DA per CPI point 1.35, 1.50, 1.65, 1.50, 1.65, 1.80, adjusted 1 April and 1 October. Order 3786-3809 of 7 December 2020 (4da.pdf) labels its base column 'Rates vide notification dated 22.10.19' with the same figures.

2026-10-17: the 2019 notification covers the classes of workers 'mentioned in all the Schedule employments as mentioned in earlier notification No. F.12(1)142/11/MW/Lab/2023-2047 dated 26th July'. That is 25 notifications (2023 to 2047), one per employment, compiled in notification_minimum_wages.pdf (214 pages; English pages 1-103 read from the text layer; printing presses, No. 2029, appears twice). Agriculture (2042) and the Delhi Transport Corporation (2030) are on the list. Brick kilns, domestic work and sales promotion are not. No employment added since 2011 was found on the department's site; the Delhi government's gazette search (it.delhigovt.nic.in) returned HTTP 503.
